name: Obadiah
overview: Obadiah was a male member of the tribe of Issachar, identified specifically as the son of Izrahiah. Beyond this unique lineage attribute, Scripture provides minimal additional personal details about him. His mention is concise, rooted firmly in genealogical records.
namesAndTitles: The name Obadiah means "servant [worshiper] of YHWH," reflecting a devotional relationship to the Lord. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God, but it carries significant theological meaning consistent with faithful service to God.
familyAndRelationships: Obadiah is explicitly recorded as the son of Izrahiah, establishing a clear paternal link within the tribe of Issachar. Scripture does not provide further family relationships beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Obadiah's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Issachar, connecting him to the broader narrative of Israel's tribal heritage. His identification as the son of Izrahiah situates him within the covenant community, underscoring the importance of lineage in God's unfolding plan. While details about his life and deeds are scarce, his inclusion in Scripture affirms the continuity of God's people through successive generations.
